Introduction
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Daily planning includes both one-time tasks and repeating habits.
Fais gives each user a private place to organize their day.
A playful routine board and calendar make progress visible.
Fais brings one-time work and repeating routines into one personal workspace. The demo uses a labeled fictional account; real accounts start empty.
Problem Statement
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Scattered notes make it easy to lose track of small commitments.
Unclear priorities make the next task difficult to choose.
Repeated routines need date-specific tracking and a useful history.
A task list alone offers limited visibility into daily consistency.
Describe these as the problems our project addresses, not a claim that every existing application lacks the features.
Objectives of the Project
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Organize tasks with clear priorities, deadlines, and status.
Track repeating routines without losing earlier completion records.
Restore saved data across refreshes and authenticated sessions.
Support desktop and mobile access with visible progress.
Explain that these objectives map to implemented modules. Priority is an explicit ordering rule. MongoDB persistence means a refresh restores confirmed data.
Scope of the Project
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Implemented: personal accounts, task CRUD, priorities, and search.
Implemented: routines, calendars, statistics, activity, and settings.
Implemented: autosave, retries, and responsive web navigation.
Excluded: Android app, notifications, offline sync, teams, and mood journal.
The application has individual accounts, not a shared team model. Mood journaling was optional and remains future scope. There is no deployed production service in this deliverable.
Existing System
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Paper lists provide a simple record, but updates and summaries are manual.
Basic digital lists organize items but vary in recurring-task support.
Modern planners already offer many advanced planning features.
Fais focuses on a coherent personal workflow and explainable MERN design.

Paper lists are useful but do not automatically synchronize or summarize data. Modern digital planners can already include advanced features. Fais is a focused full-stack implementation and learning project, not an unsupported novelty claim.
Proposed System
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
A user signs in to a MongoDB-backed session.
Tasks use High, Medium, and Low priority with deadline ordering.
Routine check-ins belong to one routine and one local calendar date.
Calendar, statistics, and activity read persisted records.
Walk through the app in order: register, plan tasks, check in to routines, inspect reports. All business data passes through Express, which applies ownership and validation rules.
Hardware and Software Requirements
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Verified environment: Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 26.6.2, Node 24.14.0, npm 11.9.0.
Required software: MongoDB 8.0, Git, a modern browser, and project dependencies.
Practical recommendation: 8 GB RAM and several GB of free disk space.
Network: package installation and optional fonts or Atlas. Compass is optional.

This lists the actual software environment and practical hardware advice, not a benchmarked minimum. MongoDB 8.0 macOS support starts at macOS 14. Compass is optional and can be installed later. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/tutorial/install-mongodb-on-os-x/ and https://vite.dev/guide/.
Technology Used
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
React + Vite: pages, reusable components, routing, and production builds.
Node.js + Express: REST endpoints, validation, and ownership checks.
MongoDB + Mongoose: records, indexes, persistence, and version checks.
bcrypt, sessions, and Luxon: password hashing, authentication, and local dates.

React renders the browser interface. Vite builds it. Express runs REST routes on Node. Mongoose connects the server to MongoDB. Supporting dependencies have specific jobs: bcrypt hashes, express-session and connect-mongo manage sessions, Luxon handles IANA timezone calculations. Official documentation links are on slide 15.
Block Diagram
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Browser / React

Forms and pages
API fetch client
Express / Node

Session + CSRF
Validation + controllers
MongoDB

Users and planning data
Sessions and history
Requests / JSON responses
Queries / results
Ownership and business rules stay on the server.

The browser never connects directly to MongoDB. The forward arrows represent requests/queries and the reverse arrows represent JSON responses/results. Express middleware verifies the session, Origin, CSRF token and ownership. The same API can support a future native client with appropriate authentication integration.
Modules of the Project
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Authentication
Registration, login, session restoration
Tasks / Priority
CRUD, filtering, status, and racing progress
Routines
Schedules, ordering, archive, and daily check-ins
Calendar / Statistics
Occurrence rates, daily counts, and streaks
Autosave / Activity
Serialized saves, retries, and action history
Settings
Name and IANA timezone

Explain how modules share a small centralized API helper and authentication context. Autosave serializes edits and retains unsaved text after a failed request. Activity is not a guaranteed transactional audit log: a failed activity write raises a visible warning after the core mutation is saved.

Future Scope
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
A native Android client that reuses the Express API.
Reminders and notifications with user-controlled scheduling.
Offline synchronization with explicit conflict handling.
Shared planning, an optional mood journal, and native widgets.

These are future possibilities, not completed features. A native Android client would reuse Express. Offline support requires a conflict and synchronization design. A mood journal and native widgets were intentionally not included in the core deliverable.
Conclusion
FAIS / FULL STACK DEVELOPMENT
Fais combines one-time tasks and repeating routines in a working MERN app.
Confirmed MongoDB data survives refreshes and session restoration.
Focused tests check isolation, date rules, ordering, and save reliability.
The project provides a foundation for further native and offline features.

Demonstrate the actual application before making claims. The tests cover ownership, priority order, routine dates/history, timezone boundaries and save failures. Avoid invented performance figures or claims of production readiness.
